items.description: Monte Verde is the highest point on Sao Vicente and rises above the eastern side of the island. It is a clear landmark for views over Mindelo and the Atlantic coast.
Cova de Paul is a volcanic crater on Santo Antao that opens into one of the island's best-known green valleys. Its sheltered shape helps create a cooler microclimate for farming and hiking.
Bordeira do Fogo is the great crater rim that frames Pico do Fogo. It forms one of the most dramatic volcanic landscapes on the island of Fogo.
Monte Trigo marks the remote western edge of Santo Antao near the Atlantic coast. The area sits by the foot of Tope de Coroa and is linked to the island's hiking routes.
facts: Close to Tarrafal de Monte Trigo

items.description: Monte Grande is the highest point on Sal and stands out on an otherwise flat island. It rises north of Espargos and is part of Sal's protected landscape.
Monte Penoso is the highest point on Maio and rises above the island's low, open terrain. The mountain belongs to the protected landscape on the eastern side of the island.
Monte Batalha is a mountain on Maio with views across the island's southern side. It is one of the smaller but named high points in the island's landscape.
Monte Sobrado rises in the volcanic highlands of Fogo. It is one of the island's prominent peaks in the Santa Catarina do Fogo area.
Monte Duarte is a high volcanic mountain on Fogo. It belongs to the rugged interior of the island and adds to the steep relief around Santa Catarina do Fogo.
facts: Part of the island's volcanic interior

items.description: Pico da Antonia is the highest mountain on Santiago and a major landmark in the island's central highlands. Its slopes shape much of the surrounding relief.
